critical_examples.text: 例题 1-1 asks whether a DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B on one H100 SXM can generate a new token within 10 ms, first at 1 byte per parameter, then comparing compute doubling, bandwidth doubling and intra-batch weight reuse.

critical_facts.text: 例题 1-1 estimation conditions: N≈70×10⁹ parameters at 1 byte per parameter → R_W=M_W≈70 GB; F≈2N≈140 GFLOPs per step; capacity stated as 73.73 GB including quant data; all weights are re-read each step.
Single-request time lower bounds: weight read 70 GB ÷ 3350 GB/s ≈ 20.90 ms; matrix compute 140 GFLOPs ÷ 989400 GFLOP/s ≈ 0.1415 ms; the read bound is about 148× the compute bound.
Intervention comparison: doubling compute gives 0.1415→0.0707 ms while the read bound stays 20.90 ms; doubling HBM bandwidth or halving weight volume lowers the read bound to ≈10.45 ms.

Batch reuse: B=8 requests share one 70 GB read while compute grows ≈8× (≈1.13 ms); per-output amortized read ≈2.61 ms; throughput 47.9→383 token/s; the per-output amortization is a batch time divided by output count, not single-request latency.

Turnpoint B*=b_WΠ/(2β)≈147.7; beyond ~148, batch time grows approximately proportionally; the turnpoint compares only matrix compute and weight read and ignores KV capacity (only ~6.27 GB free after 73.73 GB of weights, not enough for 148 requests' KV).
Arithmetic intensity I=F/R_W=2B/b_W (FLOP per byte read) is compared with the machine balance Π/β; below it the read time dominates, above it the compute time dominates.

Measurements: 1→64 requests raise batch throughput ≈31× while single-request output interval grows 26.5→40.5 ms; setup is Qwen3-8B BF16 on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (96 GB, 1.792 TB/s, 503.8 TFLOP/s dense BF16).

练习 1-3 requires: with effective bandwidth 70% and effective compute 50%, compute batch lower bounds, per-output amortized time and ideal throughput for B=1/16/64, judge the 10 ms per-request-per-step target, repeat with weight read halved at unchanged compute, find the B* where compute and read times are equal, and explain why smaller per-output amortized time does not shorten single-request step latency.

练习 1-4 requires: from the four measured concurrency levels in figures 1-13/1-14 compute throughput ratios and TPOT growth, state the ideal prediction if only the shared weight read limits growth, offer two explanations distinguishable by measurement, and design a measurement varying only context length while holding model, output length and timing points fixed.

1.3.4: by 1.792 TB/s a decode step reading weights and old KV needs at least 8.62 ms, yet batch=1 measured 26.5 ms (MBU 33%); the gap has two sources — model missing terms (lower bound rises, fix the model) or implementation overhead (host Python/driver/PCIe, removable); closing per-step logging gives 12.1 ms and accelerator-event timing gives 10.7 ms, ~20% above the bound; the check order is first model, then implementation.

Corrected claim: adding per-request state read (R_W+B·R_state,1)/β and compute B·F₁/Π both grow with B; if R_state,1/β ≥ F₁/Π there is no positive crossing, otherwise the crossing B* is larger than when state is ignored (pushed later); only adding attention-like compute to the compute term can move it earlier, and both terms added must be compared numerically.

Delivered revision's live numbers for 练习 1-3 defaults: read bound 70 GB ÷ 2.345 TB/s ≈ 29.85 ms (independent of B); B=1/16/64 batch bounds all 29.85 ms, none meeting 10 ms; per-output 29.85/1.87/0.47 ms; ideal throughput 33.5/536/2144 token/s; B*≈105.5; with the read volume halved the bound is ≈14.93 ms and at B=64 compute (18.11 ms) overtakes the read.
